Prerequisite: The FortiMail registered with Fortinet Technical Support (FortiCare), with a valid support contract that includes the service subscriptions, and each purchased service or feature license bound to its serial number; in HA, every member registered and licensed
What it enables: Service from the FortiGuard Distribution Network, and the subscriptions and feature licenses P3, P4, P7 to P9, and P11, which FortiMail checks by polling FortiCare for its serial number
How to put it in place: Register the serial number at the Fortinet Technical Support website and bind each license; check GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information widget) and GUI: System > FortiGuard > License
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Connecting to FortiGuard services" (register the unit and have a valid support contract to receive service from the FDN), "License Information widget", and "Deploying member HA" (register all units; licenses are purchased and registered for each unit)

Prerequisite: A path from the FortiMail to the FortiGuard Distribution Network (FDN): DNS servers that resolve the FortiGuard server names, a default route, and firewalls that allow FDN traffic, or an override server (such as a FortiManager) or a web proxy
What it enables: FortiGuard Antivirus engine and definition downloads, FortiGuard Antispam rating queries, outbreak queries, and other FortiGuard data such as the Internet Service Database
How to put it in place: Check the connection in GUI: System > FortiGuard > AntiSpam (a DNS or connection error is shown if the query fails), execute nslookup name <FQDN> for service.fortiguard.net, and the route in GUI: System > Network > Routing; for a web proxy, config system fortiguard antivirus; set tunneling-status enable; set tunneling-address <PROXY>; set tunneling-port <PORT>; end
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Connecting to FortiGuard services" (verifying rating query connectivity: DNS, default route, firewalls that allow FDN traffic, override server) and "Configuring FortiGuard services and licensed features"; row "Web proxy for FortiGuard antivirus updates and antispam queries"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Antivirus subscription
What it enables: Current antivirus engines and virus definitions for antivirus scanning, and virus outbreak protection queries to the FortiGuard Antivirus service
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check its status and last update in GUI: System > FortiGuard > License
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Connecting to FortiGuard services" (FortiGuard Antivirus subscribers download the most recent definitions and engine packages), "Configuring FortiGuard Antivirus service" (virus outbreak protection), and "Settings that are not synchronized by HA" (licenses are specific to each unit)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Antispam subscription
What it enables: FortiGuard Antispam queries (DNSBL of spam origins, SURBL of spam URLs, and spam checksums), the FortiGuard IP reputation check, and spam outbreak protection
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check its status in GUI: System > FortiGuard > License; the service must be enabled in GUI: System > FortiGuard > AntiSpam
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Connecting to FortiGuard services" (a connection error appears if the FortiGuard Antispam license does not exist or is expired), "About FortiGuard Antispam service queries", and "About spam outbreak protection from FortiGuard"

Prerequisite: A FortiSandbox that the FortiMail can reach: a FortiSandbox appliance or VM, or the FortiSandbox Cloud service, which needs a service entitlement license (shared or dedicated hosting) on every FortiMail in an HA cluster
What it enables: Submission of attachments and URLs for sandbox analysis, and the FortiSandbox settings that depend on it
How to put it in place: For an appliance, the FortiSandbox host name or IP address and the ports through any firewall; for the cloud service, the license, shown for FortiSandbox in GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information widget); then configure GUI: System > FortiSandbox > FortiSandbox
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Using FortiSandbox inspection" (FortiSandbox type Appliance, Cloud, or Enhanced Cloud; cloud options appear only with a valid service entitlement license; all HA members must be licensed for the cloud service)

Prerequisite: A FortiNDR system, with an API key generated on it
What it enables: FortiNDR malware detection of files submitted from antivirus profiles
How to put it in place: Enter the FortiNDR base URL and API key in GUI: System > FortiNDR > FortiNDR
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Using FortiNDR inspection"

Prerequisite: A feature license for the Fortinet Enterprise Advanced Threat Protection (ATP) bundle
What it enables: Impersonation analysis (display name and email address mapping)
How to put it in place: Purchase the bundle, register it (P1), and check it in GUI: System > FortiGuard > License
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring impersonation profiles" (a feature license for the Enterprise ATP bundle is required)

Prerequisite: An advanced management feature license
What it enables: Domain quarantines, the Header From option in access control and in recipient policies, and the other settings under config system advanced-management
How to put it in place: Purchase the license, register it (P1), and enable the feature in GUI: System > FortiGuard > Licensed Feature (Advanced Management section)
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring advanced management features" and "Searching the quarantines or samples" (domain quarantines need a valid advanced management feature license); FortiMail 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "system advanced-management" (advanced management options require a valid feature license)

Prerequisite: A cloud API feature license, with the FortiMail in gateway mode
What it enables: Assisted integration with Microsoft 365 for inline scanning through Exchange Online connectors
How to put it in place: Purchase the license and register it (P1); set the operation mode with config system global; set operation-mode gateway; end
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Integrating with Microsoft 365 via SMTP" (requires a valid feature license for cloud APIs and gateway mode) and "MS365 Inline section"

Prerequisite: A Microsoft 365 tenant (Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Entra, and Exchange Online) in which FortiMail is registered as a single-tenant application with the Exchange.ManageAsApp permission and the Exchange Administrator role, and an X.509 certificate for its app-only authentication
What it enables: Automatic creation of the inbound, outbound, and internal connectors for inline scanning
How to put it in place: Register the application in the Microsoft Azure portal, upload the certificate there, and upload the PEM certificate with its private key in GUI: System > Mail Setting > MS365 Inline
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Integrating with Microsoft 365 via SMTP" (steps 1 to 16)

Prerequisite: A FortiIdentity Cloud service license (paid, owned by the same account as the FortiMail, or a trial for up to three seats)
What it enables: One-time token codes and FortiToken Mobile push approvals for administrator multi-factor authentication
How to put it in place: Purchase the license and register it (P1), or activate the trial next to FortiIdentity Cloud in the License Information widget in GUI: Dashboard > Status
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring administrator accounts" (Two Factor Authentication: only FortiIdentity Cloud is supported, and it requires a valid paid or trial service license)

Prerequisite: DNS servers that the FortiMail can query, preferably on the local network
What it enables: MX and PTR lookups (reverse DNS and forged IP check), SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and ARC checks, DNSBL and SURBL queries, DANE and MTA-STS checks, SMTP domain checks, and the alert email that the FortiMail sends
How to put it in place: config system dns; set primary <DNS1>; set secondary <DNS2>; end or GUI: System > Network > DNS
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring DNS" (DNS servers are required for MX lookups, PTR lookups, FortiGuard connectivity, DKIM sender authentication, and more) and "Configuring alert email" (alert email requires at least one DNS server); rows of the feature map

Prerequisite: Public DNS records: an MX record for each protected domain that names the FortiMail as its mail gateway (with the other MX records removed in gateway mode), an A record for the FortiMail host name, and a reverse DNS (PTR) record for its public IP address
What it enables: Delivery of external mail to and through the FortiMail, so that it cannot be bypassed, and reverse DNS checks of its outgoing mail
How to put it in place: Create the records on the authoritative public DNS servers of each protected domain (not a FortiMail setting)
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring DNS records for the protected domains" and the operation mode comparison (a DNS MX record change is required in gateway and server mode)

Prerequisite: The DKIM public key of each signing selector published in a TXT record on the authoritative public DNS server of the domain
What it enables: Validation of FortiMail's DKIM signatures by the recipients' mail servers
How to put it in place: Create or import the key pair in GUI: Domain & User > Domain > Domain (DKIM and ARC Setting), download the public key, publish it in the domain's DNS, wait for it to propagate, and then activate the key
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "DKIM and ARC Setting" (put the public key in the TXT record; recipients cannot validate signatures until it propagates)

Prerequisite: The protected domains, each with its protected SMTP server (the mail server to which the FortiMail delivers the domain's mail)
What it enables: Recipient-based policies for incoming mail, domain-level administrators, and recipient address verification against the mail server
How to put it in place: GUI: Domain & User > Domain > Domain
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring protected domains", "Recipient Address Verification section", and "Controlling email based on sender and recipient email addresses"; row "Protected domains"

Prerequisite: A policy or rule that applies the profile: an IP-based or recipient-based policy (session, antispam, antivirus, content, DLP, resource, and authentication profiles, and the action profiles that they use), an access control or delivery rule (TLS profiles), or a delivery rule or content action profile (encryption profiles)
What it enables: The profile's settings, which take effect only on the mail and SMTP sessions that the policy or rule governs
How to put it in place: config policy ip; edit <ID>; set status enable; set profile-session <SESSION_PROFILE>; set profile-antispam <AS_PROFILE>; set profile-antivirus <AV_PROFILE>; set profile-content <CONTENT_PROFILE>; next; end, config policy recipient; edit <ID>; set status enable; set profile-dlp <DLP_PROFILE>; next; end, and config policy access-control delivery; edit <RULE>; set tls-profile <TLS_PROFILE>; next; end
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring profiles" (a profile is applied directly in a policy or by inclusion in another profile that a policy selects), "Configuring TLS security profiles" and "Configuring encryption profiles" (where each is applied); rows "IP-based policies", "Recipient-based policies", and "Access control delivery rules"

Prerequisite: The DoD PKI on the FortiMail: the DoD root and intermediate CA certificates, current certificate revocation lists, and the OCSP responder certificates, plus the CA certificates of any server whose certificate the FortiMail must validate
What it enables: Validation of administrator and user certificates, of the certificates presented by mail servers, syslog servers, and RADIUS servers over TLS, of S/MIME certificates, and signing of the FortiMail's own certificate requests
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Certificate > CA Certificate; GUI: System > Certificate > Certificate Revocation List; GUI: System > Certificate > Remote (OCSP responder certificates)
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Managing certificate authority certificates", "Managing the certificate revocation list", "Configuring certificate bindings" (the signing CA certificate must be uploaded first), "Configuring logging" (with TCP over TLS the syslog server must present a valid certificate), and "Configuring TLS security profiles" (Secure requires a certificate-authenticated connection)

Prerequisite: A certificate issued to the FortiMail by a DoD CA, with its private key, in the local certificate store
What it enables: The certificate that the FortiMail presents for the web UI and its secure connections, and as a client certificate to an LDAP server
How to put it in place: Generate a certificate signing request and import the signed certificate in GUI: System > Certificate > Local Certificate
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Managing local certificates" (FortiMail requires a local server certificate to prove its identity when clients request secure connections) and "Configuring LDAP profiles" (client certificate)

Prerequisite: S/MIME certificate bindings: the certificate (and, for decryption and signing, the private key) of each sender or recipient address or domain, and an S/MIME-capable destination gateway, mail server, or client
What it enables: S/MIME encryption, decryption, and signing by encryption profiles
How to put it in place: GUI: Encryption > S/MIME > Certificate Binding
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Using S/MIME encryption" and "Configuring certificate bindings"

Prerequisite: The identity-based encryption (IBE) service enabled, with its service name and base URL
What it enables: IBE encryption of mail for external recipients and fallback to IBE when TLS fails
How to put it in place: config system encryption ibe; set status enable; set service-name "<IBE_SERVICE_NAME>"; set url-base "<BASE_URL>"; end or GUI: Encryption > IBE > IBE Encryption
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring IBE services"; FortiMail 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "system encryption ibe"

Prerequisite: An administrator access profile with the least privilege the administrator needs
What it enables: Local administrator accounts that are assigned the profile
How to put it in place: config system accprofile; edit <PROFILE>; config menuitem; edit system_grp; set permission read; next; end; next; end
Source: Row "Access profiles (none, read, read-update, read-write per functional area)"

Prerequisite: An LDAP directory server (such as Microsoft Active Directory) reachable from the FortiMail, with a bind account for queries
What it enables: LDAP authentication of administrators, LDAP group and user lookups in policies and rules, and sender identity checks
How to put it in place: config profile ldap; edit <LDAP>; set server <LDAP_SERVER>; set secure ssl; next; end or GUI: Profile > LDAP > LDAP
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring LDAP profiles"; rows "Remote administrator authentication with LDAP" and "Client certificate authentication in LDAP profiles"

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server reachable from the FortiMail, with the FortiMail added as a client with a shared secret (and, for secure RADIUS, a server certificate over TLS)
What it enables: RADIUS authentication of administrators and authentication failover to a second RADIUS server
How to put it in place: config profile authentication radius; edit <RADIUS>; set server <RADIUS_SERVER>; set secret <SECRET>; next; end or GUI: Profile > Authentication > RADIUS
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring authentication profiles"; rows "Remote administrator authentication with RADIUS" and "Secure (TLS) RADIUS"

Prerequisite: An SMTP, IMAP, or POP3 server (usually the protected mail server) that authenticates email users
What it enables: SMTP authentication of email users and authentication failover to a second server address
How to put it in place: config profile authentication smtp; edit <AUTH_PROFILE>; set server <MAIL_SERVER>; next; end or GUI: Profile > Authentication > SMTP
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring authentication profiles"; row "SMTP authentication of email users"

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider (IdP) with the FortiMail registered as a service provider
What it enables: SAML single sign-on for the administrator GUI and webmail
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Single Sign On > Setting
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring single sign-on (SSO)"; rows "Multiple identity providers for SAML SSO" and "Separate SAML service providers for the administrator GUI and webmail"

Prerequisite: A syslog server reachable from the FortiMail that supports TCP with octet counting or TCP over TLS (with a valid server certificate for TLS)
What it enables: Off-loading of event, history, antivirus, and antispam logs to a central log server
How to put it in place: GUI: Log & Report > Log Setting > Remote
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring logging" (Protocol Syslog and Mode TCP or TCP over TLS); row "Remote syslog servers (TCP over TLS)"

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer that accepts logs from the FortiMail
What it enables: Logging to FortiAnalyzer over OFTPS, reliable logging, and mail delivery status on FortiAnalyzer
How to put it in place: config log setting remote; edit <FAZ>; set status enable; set server <FAZ_IP>; set protocol oftps; next; end or GUI: Log & Report > Log Setting > Remote
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring logging" (Protocol OFTPS: FortiAnalyzer only); row "Logging to FortiAnalyzer (OFTPS)"

Prerequisite: Alert email recipients and categories
What it enables: Alert email when the hard disk monitor detects a problem
How to put it in place: config log alertemail recipient; edit <ISSO_EMAIL>; next; end; config log alertemail setting; set categories diskfull ha remote-storage-failure system virus; end
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring alert email" (both recipients and categories must be configured); row "Alert email (disk full, HA, system, virus, remote storage failure)"

Prerequisite: NTP servers reachable from the FortiMail (up to ten), preferably internal, authoritative time sources
What it enables: Synchronized system time for log time stamps
How to put it in place: config system time ntp; set ntpsync enable; set ntpserver <NTP_SERVER>; end or GUI: System > Configuration > Time
Source: FortiMail 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "system time ntp"; row "System time and NTP synchronization"

Prerequisite: An SNMP manager that supports SNMPv3, with matching user accounts
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and traps with authentication and privacy
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Configuration > SNMP
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring SNMP users" (SNMP v3 also requires that you define SNMP managers)

Prerequisite: An SCP, SFTP, FTP, or TFTP server reachable from the FortiMail
What it enables: Firmware installation from a file server and manual and scheduled configuration backups
How to put it in place: The server and an account on it (not a FortiMail setting); then, for example, execute backup full-config scp <FILE> <SERVER>
Source: FortiMail 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "backup", "restore image", and "system scheduled-backup"; rows "Firmware upgrade (web UI, FTP, SCP, or TFTP)" and "Configuration backup (manual and scheduled)"

Prerequisite: The other FortiMail units of the HA cluster: the same firmware version and operation mode, each registered and licensed separately (P1), heartbeat links between them, and firewalls that allow the HA ports
What it enables: HA failover and configuration synchronization
How to put it in place: GUI: System > High Availability > Configuration (on each unit, after setting the same operation mode and firmware on all of them)
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Deploying member HA" (register all units, same firmware version and operation mode), "Settings that are not synchronized by HA" (licenses and operation mode), and "About HA port numbers and protocols"

Prerequisite: A FIPS-certified FortiMail firmware build on supported hardware, and a complete backup taken before FIPS-CC mode is enabled (enabling or disabling it erases the configuration)
What it enables: FIPS-CC mode and its cryptographic self-tests
How to put it in place: Obtain the certified build from Fortinet Technical Support, then back up with execute backup full-config scp <FILE> <SERVER>
Source: FortiMail 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "system fips-cc" (valid only with a FIPS-certified firmware build on supported hardware; all existing configuration is lost when the mode changes)

Prerequisite: FIPS-CC mode enabled
What it enables: Valid results from the FIPS known answer tests
How to put it in place: config system fips-cc; set status fips-ciphers; end
Source: FortiMail 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "fips kat" (results are valid only if FIPS-CC mode is enabled and configured); row "FIPS-CC mode"

Prerequisite: A FortiMail model with a front LCD panel
What it enables: PIN protection of the LCD panel buttons
How to put it in place: Model capability (check the model's hardware documentation)
Source: FortiMail 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "system global" (lcd-protection and lcd-pin: the PIN protects the buttons on the front LCD panel)

Prerequisite: A FortiMail model that supports RAID, with enough hard disks for the RAID level
What it enables: Redundant storage of logs and mail
How to put it in place: Model capability; configure it in GUI: System > RAID (the menu is not shown on models without RAID)
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring RAID and self-encrypting drives (SED)" and "About RAID levels" (supported RAID levels vary by model; some models do not support RAID)

Prerequisite: A FortiMail 900G with self-encrypting drives, and an encryption key set on the drives
What it enables: SED encryption and auto lock of the mail and log disks
How to put it in place: Model capability; after RAID setup, set the key and enable encryption with the CLI commands given in the Administration Guide (they are not in the 8.0.0 CLI Reference)
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Self-encrypting drives" (FortiMail 900G supports SED; an encryption key must be set before encryption is enabled)

Prerequisite: A STIX/TAXII threat feed server reachable from the FortiMail, with an account if it requires authentication
What it enables: Threat feed imports of IP addresses, malware hashes, and URL categories
How to put it in place: config system threat-feed; edit <FEED>; set status enable; set resource-url <FEED_URL>; set server-identity-check full; next; end or GUI: Security > Threat Feed > Threat Feed
Source: FortiMail 8.0.2 Administration Guide, "Configuring a threat feed"; row "STIX/TAXII threat feeds"
